SOFTWARE TESTING
(According to Roger S. Pressman – Software Engineering: A Practitioner’s Approach, 7th Edition)
1. Introduction to Software Testing
Definition (Pressman)
Software testing is a set of activities that can be planned in advance and conducted systematically to
detect errors in software so that defects can be removed before the product is delivered to the
customer.
Pressman states that testing is not the process of showing that software works correctly, but the
process of executing a program with the intent of finding errors.
Fundamental Principles of Testing (Pressman)
Pressman defines the following fundamental testing principles:

process of executing a program with the intent of finding errors.
Fundamental Principles of Testing (Pressman)
Pressman defines the following fundamental testing principles:
Testing demonstrates the presence of defects, not their absence.
Exhaustive testing is not possible.
Testing should begin early in the software life cycle.
Defect clustering occurs (a small number of modules contain most defects).
Testing is context dependent.
The absence-of-errors fallacy: software that is defect-free but does not meet user needs is still
unacceptable.
Purpose / Objectives
To uncover errors introduced during development
To verify that software conforms to specified requirements
To validate that software meets user expectations
To reduce the cost of defects by detecting them early

2. Verification vs Validation
Verification (Pressman)
Verification refers to the set of activities that ensure that software correctly implements a specific
function.

➡ “Are we building the product right?”
Validation (Pressman)
Validation refers to a different set of activities that ensure that the software built is traceable to
customer requirements.

3. Levels of Testing
Pressman defines testing as a process executed in levels, where each level has specific objectives.
3(a). Unit Testing
Definition (Pressman)
Unit testing focuses on individual software components, testing each unit independently to ensure it
performs as designed.
Purpose / Objectives
To uncover errors in logic and data structures
To test boundary conditions
To verify correct operation of individual modules
Where It Is Used
Lowest level of testing
Performed immediately after coding
Simple Example

To test boundary conditions
To verify correct operation of individual modules
Where It Is Used
Lowest level of testing
Performed immediately after coding
Simple Example
Testing a function that calculates total price by giving different input values.
Important Exam Lines
Unit testing concentrates on functional correctness of individual modules.
Test cases are derived from module specifications.
3(b). Integration Testing
Definition (Pressman)
Integration testing is a systematic technique for constructing the software architecture while
conducting tests to uncover errors associated with interfacing.
Purpose / Objectives

To detect interface defects
To verify communication between modules
To ensure combined modules work together correctly
Types of Integration Testing
1. Top-Down Integration Testing
Main control module tested first
Subordinate modules integrated progressively
Uses stubs to simulate lower-level modules

Types of Integration Testing
1. Top-Down Integration Testing
Main control module tested first
Subordinate modules integrated progressively
Uses stubs to simulate lower-level modules
2. Bottom-Up Integration Testing
Low-level modules tested first
Modules grouped into clusters
Uses drivers to simulate higher-level modules
3. Sandwich (Hybrid) Testing
Combination of top-down and bottom-up approaches
Critical modules tested early
Simple Example
Testing interaction between login module and database module.
Important Exam Lines
“Integration testing focuses on errors related to interfaces.”
Use of stubs and drivers is characteristic.
3(c). Validation Testing
Definition (Pressman)
Validation testing succeeds when software functions in a manner that can be reasonably expected by
the customer.
Purpose / Objectives
To ensure software meets all functional requirements

Acceptance Testing (Part of Validation Testing)
Definition
Acceptance testing is conducted by the customer to determine whether to accept or reject the system.
Types
Alpha testing (at developer’s site)
Beta testing (at customer’s site)
Simple Example
Client tests a university portal before final delivery.
Important Exam Lines
“Validation testing answers the question: Is the software acceptable to the customer?”
3(d). System Testing
Definition (Pressman)
System testing tests the entire system after integration to ensure it satisfies system requirements.
Types of System Testing
1. Recovery Testing
Evaluates system’s ability to recover from crashes or failures
2. Security Testing
Verifies protection mechanisms against unauthorized access
3. Stress Testing

4. White-Box Testing
Definition (Pressman)
White-box testing is a testing technique that examines the internal logic and structure of the code.
Objectives
Ensure all independent paths are executed
Exercise logical decisions
Verify internal data structures
Techniques
1. Basis Path Testing
Uses control flow graph
Ensures execution of all independent paths
2. Condition Testing
Tests logical conditions in the program
3. Loop Testing

2. Condition Testing

3. Loop Testing

4. Data Flow Testing
Tracks variables from definition to usage
Important Exam Line
“White-box testing derives test cases from program logic.”
5. Black-Box Testing

Definition (Pressman)
Black-box testing focuses on functional requirements, without regard to internal program structure.
Objectives
Validate input/output behavior
Detect missing or incorrect functions
Identify interface errors
Techniques
1. Equivalence Partitioning
Divides input data into valid and invalid classes
2. Boundary Value Analysis
Tests values at the edges of input ranges
3. Cause-Effect Graphing
Identifies logical relationships between inputs and outputs

3. Cause-Effect Graphing

Important Exam Line
“Black-box testing is also called behavioral testing.”
6. Regression Testing
Definition (Pressman)
Regression testing is the re-execution of a subset of tests to ensure that changes have not introduced
new errors.
Purpose
Detect unintended side effects
Ensure existing functionality remains intact
Relation with Integration Testing
Performed whenever modules are integrated or modified

Definition (Pressman)
Smoke testing is a preliminary testing activity that checks whether the basic functions of the software
work correctly.
Purpose

7. Smoke Testing
Definition (Pressman)
Smoke testing is a preliminary testing activity that checks whether the basic functions of the software
work correctly.
Purpose
Verify stability of build
Decide whether further testing is possible
When It Is Performed
After receiving a new software build
Example
Checking if application launches and main menu loads.
Important Exam Line
“Smoke testing is a confidence-building step.”
8. Debugging
Difference Between Testing and Debugging (Pressman)
Testing
Debugging
Detects errors
Removes errors
Preventive
Corrective

Unpredictable process

CONCLUSION (Exam Note)
Pressman emphasizes that software testing is a critical quality assurance activity, executed in a
structured manner across multiple levels to ensure reliability, correctness, and customer satisfaction.
